title: Career Roadmap: E-Commerce Executive
summary: An E-Commerce Executive helps manage the day-to-day operations of an online business. Responsibilities may include uploading products, maintaining product information, coordinating orders, monitoring inventory, managing promotions, resolving customer issues and tracking sales performance.

about.label: Core Focus
about.text: Online store operations, product listings, order processing, customer service, promotions and sales performance

about.label: Work Settings
about.text: E-commerce companies, online retailers, D2C brands, marketplaces, digital agencies and retail businesses

about.label: Suitable For
about.text: Students interested in online business, digital marketing, product management, analytics and customer experience

blocks.text: An E-Commerce Executive helps manage the day-to-day operations of an online business. Responsibilities may include uploading products, maintaining product information, coordinating orders, monitoring inventory, managing promotions, resolving customer issues and tracking sales performance.

The role combines business operations, digital marketing, data analysis and customer experience. With experience, professionals can progress into marketplace management, e-commerce operations, performance marketing, category management or online business management.

rows.text: E-Commerce Executive, Marketplace Executive, Product Listing Executive
E-Commerce Operations Specialist, Catalog Executive, Online Sales Executive
Marketplace Manager, E-Commerce Operations Analyst, Category Executive
E-Commerce Manager, Marketplace Growth Manager, Digital Commerce Specialist
Head of E-Commerce, Online Business Manager, Digital Commerce Lead
D2C brand owner, online store operator, marketplace seller

blocks.text: Progression depends on demonstrated results, platform expertise, analytical ability and the scale of the business.

sections.heading: Step-by-Step Roadmap During the B.Voc Degree

blocks.text: The following plan can be adapted to a three-year B.Voc programme. Adjust it to match the actual semester structure and internship requirements of the institution.

blocks.label: Year 1
blocks.text: Business and Digital Commerce Fundamentals

blocks.label: Goal
blocks.text: Understand how online businesses operate and how customers discover and purchase products.

rows.text: Business models, revenue, costs, profit margins and customer value
B2C, B2B, D2C, marketplace and subscription models
SEO, social media marketing, email marketing and online advertising basics
Product attributes, categories, pricing and product descriptions
Customer journeys, customer support and complaint handling
Data entry, sorting, filtering, formulas and basic charts
Professional emails, reports, presentations and customer responses

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Analyse the online shopping journey of a familiar retail brand.
Prepare product descriptions for 10 sample products.
Create a spreadsheet containing product names, SKUs, prices, categories and stock levels.
Compare the product pages of three competing online stores.
Draft customer-service responses for order delays, returns and refunds.

blocks.label: Year 1 outcome
blocks.text: Understand online retail operations and maintain an organized product catalogue.

blocks.label: Year 2
blocks.text: E-Commerce Platforms and Operations

blocks.label: Goal
blocks.text: Learn to operate an online store and manage its daily workflow.

rows.text: Product creation, collections, categories, navigation and store settings
Listing management, order workflows, returns and seller performance
SKUs, product variants, images, attributes and descriptions
Stock reconciliation, reorder levels and out-of-stock monitoring
Order confirmation, fulfilment tracking, cancellations and returns
Campaign calendars, discount offers, email campaigns and social promotions
Conversion rate, average order value, revenue and abandoned-cart analysis
Payment status, shipping coordination, delivery tracking and reconciliation basics

blocks.text: Platforms to explore

items.text: Shopify or WooCommerce for online store management.
Amazon Seller Central or other relevant marketplace seller portals.
Google Analytics 4 for website traffic and conversion analysis.
Google Sheets or Excel for catalogue and order reporting.
Canva for basic promotional creatives.
Email marketing platforms for customer communication campaigns.

blocks.text: Platform access and features vary by account type. Students can use demonstrations, sandbox environments or a practice store when live seller access is unavailable.

blocks.label: Year 2 outcome
blocks.text: Manage a practice online store, maintain product data and understand the order-to-delivery process.

blocks.label: Year 3
blocks.text: Analytics, Growth and Industry Experience

blocks.label: Goal
blocks.text: Become job-ready through an internship and measurable e-commerce projects.

rows.text: Analyse revenue, orders, margins and conversion trends
Interpret traffic, campaign performance and customer acquisition data
Improve product titles, descriptions, categories and product recommendations
Track fulfilment delays, stock discrepancies and returns
Understand repeat purchases, loyalty programmes and customer feedback
Build weekly and monthly business performance reports
Work with an online retailer, marketplace seller, D2C brand or digital agency
Practise interviews, case studies and business presentations

blocks.text: Recommended final-year projects

items.text: Launch a demonstration online store for a fictional or approved small business.
Create and optimize a catalogue of 50–100 sample products.
Build an e-commerce sales dashboard using Excel or Power BI.
Analyse the reasons behind abandoned carts using a sample dataset.
Prepare a marketplace listing optimization plan for a product category.
Design a 30-day promotional calendar for a D2C brand.
Create a returns and customer-support tracking system.
Develop a competitor analysis report for an online retail category.

blocks.label: Year 3 outcome
blocks.text: Demonstrate the ability to manage catalogue data, coordinate operational workflows and interpret basic business performance metrics.
An E-Commerce Executive should understand both the operational workflow and the commercial results of an online business.

rows.text: A unique identifier used to track a product or variant
Percentage of website sessions or visitors that result in a purchase, depending on the defined measurement
Revenue divided by the number of orders
Share of shopping carts or checkout processes that do not result in a purchase, based on the measurement method
Share of orders or items returned, using a clearly defined denominator
Revenue minus cost of goods sold, expressed as a monetary amount or percentage
Marketing and sales acquisition costs divided by the number of new customers acquired
Proportion of customers who purchase again within a defined period
Frequency or proportion of demand affected by unavailable inventory
Time taken to process and fulfil an order

blocks.text: Essential calculations

blocks.label: Conversion rate
blocks.text: Purchases ÷ sessions × 100

blocks.label: Average order value
blocks.text: Revenue ÷ orders

blocks.label: Gross margin percentage
blocks.text: (Revenue − cost of goods sold) ÷ revenue × 100

blocks.label: Return rate
blocks.text: Returned orders ÷ total orders × 100, when using an order-based definition

blocks.label: Marketing ROAS
blocks.text: Revenue attributed to advertising ÷ advertising spend

blocks.label: Example
blocks.text: If a store records ₹1,00,000 in revenue from 200 orders, its average order value is ₹500.
ROAS is not the same as profit. Product costs, fulfilment, discounts, returns and other expenses also affect profitability.

blocks.text: Some employers combine these responsibilities in one position, while larger organizations maintain separate operations, marketing and analytics teams.

blocks.text: Admission to degree programmes depends on the institution's eligibility rules, credit recognition and entry requirements.

blocks.label: E-commerce operations

blocks.label: Performance marketing

blocks.label: E-commerce analytics

blocks.label: Category management

items.text: Explain how an online store or marketplace operates.
Build and maintain a structured product catalogue.
Understand inventory, order fulfilment, cancellation and returns workflows.
Operate a practice online store.

Present a practical e-commerce project with findings and recommendations.
Demonstrate internship or project experience relevant to the job.

blocks.text: For this B.Voc pathway, the strongest starting combination is e-commerce platform operations + catalogue management + Excel reporting + marketplace knowledge + customer experience.

Students who enjoy data can develop toward analytics and business intelligence. Those who enjoy marketing can move toward performance marketing and growth. Those who prefer coordination and process improvement can specialize in operations, fulfilment or marketplace management.

The key graduation outcome should be a portfolio that proves the student can manage products, understand orders, measure performance and improve an online business workflow—not merely list digital marketing certificates.
